records.central_bank: National Bank of Serbia (Narodna banka Srbije)
records.people: National Bank of Serbia management and staff borrowers (unnamed in the report); Dr Bojana Mitrovic, Vice-President of the State Audit Institution, who signed the report
records.summary: Serbia's State Audit Institution audited the National Bank of Serbia's 2016 accounts and regularity of operations and issued a Priority 1 (high) recommendation over the bank's own housing loans to its employees: claims outstanding at 31 December 2016 stood at 685,711 thousand dinars, 114 loans carried statutory default interest of 3,166 thousand dinars, a Commission was set up from 1 August 2016 to deal with borrowers not meeting their contractual obligations, and although the bank's General Affairs Directorate began registering mortgages, only two borrowers had registered one during 2016 and the bank itself had still not registered the mortgages by the close of the audit, although the loan contracts explicitly required security. The report, signed on 19 October 2017, also set a Priority 1 recommendation on reconciling the bank's book stock of finished products held by the Interior Ministry's commission agent with the actual stock. A value adjustment of 14,524 thousand dinars was made on the employee housing claims. The DRI's Priority 1 label is defined in the report as errors and irregularities indicating an immediate risk of incorrect or irregular payments, or a risk that public funds are not protected.
records.detail: This is a second, separate Serbian episode from the 2006 arrest of vice-governor Dejan Simic already on the map: a different year, a different subject (the bank's own employee housing loan book and stock reconciliation), and a different document, namely the State Audit Institution's own per-entity audit report on the central bank. The audit covers the part of the bank's operations relating to the use of public funds and to dealings with the state budget. The DRI's reports index (dri.rs/izvestaji) lists the National Bank of Serbia, Belgrade as audit subject number 1071 with nine audit reports covering financial years 2009 to 2017, so this is an annual per-entity audit series. The report for the following year, financial year 2017 (report dated 9 November 2018, dri.rs/izvestaj/1207), records no findings at any of the three priority levels, and confirms that the bank filed its response report on 22 January 2018 and that the DRI's post-audit report of 19 February 2018 rated the corrective measures satisfactory. All figures, dates and the signing officer's name above appear in the PDF at source_url.
records.quote: Препоручује се Народној банци Србије да у циљу наплате доспелих потраживања по кредитима/зајмовима интензивира активности за упис хипотека

blanks.kind: confirmed blank (inversion test) on the per-entity audit-report series; the Skyrsla til Althingis series is not reached
blanks.note: Rikisendurskodun's own published-reports index was opened and enumerated, not searched for. https://www.rikisendurskodun.is/skyrslur has a GET form with three filters (searchString1 year, searchString2 publication type, searchString3). Filtering type = 'Endurskodunarskyrsla' (value 2) with 'Oll ar' (all years) and paging through pageIndex=1..8 (https://www.rikisendurskodun.is/skyrslur?pageIndex=N&CurrentFilter1=0&CurrentFilter2=1&CurrentFilter3=0) returns 126 per-entity audit reports, covering financial years 2016 to 2021. The titles were extracted in full and read: they name ministries, universities, hospitals, police districts, sheriffs, funds, the Competition Authority, Bankasysla rikisins (the State Financial Investments agency) and the Landspitali, and Sedlabanki Islands is ABSENT from the entire list. That is the inversion test: the institution that is the central bank's statutory auditor publishes an entity-by-entity audit report series and the central bank is not in it, so there is no published Rikisendurskodun audit report on the Central Bank of Iceland in that series. What is NOT closed: the second publication category on the same index, 'Skyrsla til Althingis' (searchString2=2), was not enumerated, and the free-text search at /leit renders its results in JavaScript and returned only the static filter page to curl (two different query strings returned byte-identical 20,763-byte pages, so nothing was tested there). althingi.is is behind a Cloudflare interstitial to curl (HTTP 403, 5,504 bytes on /altext/144/s/1001.html) and should be tried with WebFetch next round. One further unopened lead below.

leads_not_opened.lead: Eight unopened DRI per-entity audit reports on the National Bank of Serbia. Listing: https://www.dri.rs/izvestaji?subjects=1071 . Report pages: /izvestaj/809 (FY2015), /izvestaj/510 (FY2014), /izvestaj/54 (FY2013), /izvestaj/157 (FY2012), /izvestaj/311 (FY2011), /izvestaj/346 (FY2010), /izvestaj/369 (FY2009). Each page carries a direct PDF link under 'Izvestaj'; percent-encode the filename. Also unopened: the DRI's post-audit report (poslerevizioni izvestaj) number 400-297/2017-07/10 of 19 February 2018 on the bank's corrective measures, and the DRI's 'Registar preporuka' pages for 2023 and 2024, which would show whether the bank has any open recommendations now.

notes: Fetches used: 3 WebSearch plus about 27 curl calls, mostly cheap HTML index pages on two hosts. No shared rate limit was reported. One record filed (SRB). Three of the fourteen assigned countries (THA, TON, WSM) already hold two case records each in have_cases.json and so are not on the live exactly-one list; that is flagged in blanks rather than worked. Iceland, the assignment's strongest lead, is now a documented blank by the inversion test rather than an untested country: Rikisendurskodun's own 126-report per-entity audit series was enumerated in full and the central bank is absent from it, which is a real finding about the project's assumption that the statutory auditor must hold per-entity material on its own central bank. Serbia's DRI, by contrast, turned out to publish exactly the annual per-entity series brief_depth.md describes, nine reports deep on the National Bank of Serbia, and eight of those nine are still unopened.
